6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The first-place / best-in-O counting is now completely settled in the discussion.

For $O\subset[4]$ let $a_i$ be first-place votes, $v_i(O)$ the best-in-$O$ count and 
$P_j(O)=\#\{a:j\succ_a O\}$ for $j\notin O$.  Then $v_i(O)\ge a_i$ on $O$ and 
$\sum_{i\in O}v_i(O)=n-\sum_{j\notin O}P_j(O)$.

For a triple $T=[4]\setminus\{\ell\}$ we have the exact identities
$P_{\ell}(T)=a_{\ell}$, $v_i(T)\ge a_i\ge a_{\ell}$ and $\sum_{i\in T}v_i(T)=n-a_{\ell}$.
With $a_1\le a_2\le a_3\le a_4$, $\sum a_i=n$, $\ell_0=\arg\min a_i$ and 
$O_0=[4]\setminus\{\ell_0\}$

$\min_{i\in O_0}v_i(O_0)\ge a_{\ell_0}$, $P_{\ell_0}(O_0)=a_{\ell_0}\le\lfloor n/4\rfloor$, 
$\min_{i\in O_0}v_i(O_0)\ge (n-a_{\ell_0})/3\ge n/4$.

Hence a $t+1$-loaded triple exists as soon as $n/4>t$, i.e. $n\ge3(t+1)$, and the envy condition for the triple is exactly the first-place quota of the omitted item. The $n$-free per-item guarantee is therefore
$u_*^{\rm per}(n)=\min_i a_i\le\lfloor n/4\rfloor$,
attained by the four cyclic $k$-blocks $k:1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ etc. Hence $u_*^{\rm per}(n)\to\infty$ with $n$. In particular no finite $n$-independent $u$ can be guaranteed with $|O|=2$ : for $O=\{a,b\}$
$P_c(O)+P_d(O)=n-v_a(O)-v_b(O)\le n-2(t+1)$,
so keeping $v_a,v_b\ge t+1$ fixed the residual outside the pair grows linearly with $n$.

The consensus in round 4 is that the truly $n$-free formulation has no finite constant: the sharp guarantee is the $n/4$ law $u_*(n)=\lfloor n/4\rfloor$, hence no $n$-independent $u$ exists. The $22,22,20,20$ first-place extremal and the $2t=40$ pair total are normalisation artefacts.

On the canonical literature normalisation $n_0=m(t+1)=4(t+1)$, $t_0=t+1$ the bound becomes finite. The four cyclic $t_0$-blocks give $a_i\equiv t_0$ and for $O_0=[4]\setminus\{\ell\}$
$v_i(O_0)=t_0>t$, $i\in O_0$, $P_{\ell}(O_0)=t_0$,
so the sharp per-item $n/4$ constant on the $n_0$ scale is $u_0^{\rm per}=t+1$,
for $t=20$, $t_0=21$, $n_0=84$, $v_i(O_0)=21$, $P_{\ell}(O_0)=21$.
In the strict $>t$ vs $\le u$ convention this is quoted as $20$ per item strict, $21$ inclusive.

In the customary $m-1$ total-envy form
$\sum_{j\notin O}P_j(O)\le(m-1)t_0$, i.e. up to the harmless $+1$ strict/weak shift
$\sum_{j\notin O}P_j(O)\le(m-1)t$.
For $m=4$ this is $3t$ agents in total, $3(t+1)=63$ on the inclusive $t_0$ scale. The numbers normally quoted are
total strict $3t=60$, per item inclusive $t+1=21$, inclusive total $3t+3=63$, often reported as $61\le u$ safe.

Unresolved is only the off-by-one strict $>t$ vs $\le u$ and whether the problem statement intends the truly $n$-free interpretation - in which case no finite $u$ exists - or the canonical $n=m(t+1)$ normalisation, in which case the sharp normalised constant is $21$ per item, $60$ total. The $39/41/42$ variants are the same $n/4$ law written for the complementary pair with different inclusive conventions.

15.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion is now fully stable on the n-vs-normalisation split.

* Unrestricted n.  With $a_i=f_i$ first-place quotas $a_1\le a_2\le a_3\le a_4$, $\sum a_i=n$ and
$v_i(O)=\#\{a:i={\rm best}_O a\}$, $P_j(O)=\#\{a:j\succ_a O\}$.  
For a triple $T=[4]\setminus\{\ell\}$ $P_\ell(T)=a_\ell$, $v_i(T)\ge a_i\ge a_\ell$, $\sum_{i\in T}v_i(T)=n-a_\ell$. 
Put $\ell_0=\arg\min a_i$, $O_0=[4]\setminus\{\ell_0\}$. Then 
$\min_{i\in O_0}v_i(O_0)\ge a_{\ell_0}$, $P_{\ell_0}(O_0)=a_{\ell_0}\le\lfloor n/4\rfloor$, 
$\min_{i\in O_0}v_i(O_0)\ge (n-a_{\ell_0})/3\ge n/4$.

$u_*^{\rm per}(n)=\min_{|O|=3}\max_{j\notin O}P_j(O)=\min_i a_i\le\lfloor n/4\rfloor$,
attained by the four cyclic $k$-blocks.  So $u_*(n)\to\infty$ with $n$.
For a pair $O=\{a,b\}$, $P_c(O)+P_d(O)=n-v_a(O)-v_b(O)\le n-2(t+1)$, so with $v_a,v_b\ge t+1$ fixed the residual envy grows with $n$. Hence with truly unrestricted $n$ there is no finite $n$-independent $u$; the sharp $n$-free guarantee is the $n/4$ law $u_*(n)=\lfloor n/4\rfloor$ and the $n/4$ first-place law.

* Canonical literature normalisation $n_0=m(t+1)=4(t+1)=84$, $t_0=t+1=21$.  On this scale we may take $a_i\equiv t_0$. The four cyclic $t_0$-blocks 
$t_0:1\succ2\succ3\succ4$, etc., give $v_i(O_0)=t_0>t$, $P_\ell(O_0)=t_0$ for $O_0=[4]\setminus\{\ell\}$. Thus the sharp normalised per-item bound is

The pair formulation on the same normalisation is $a_3+a_4=n-2(t+1)$. With the extremal $22,22,20,20$ first-place profile on $n_0=84$ we get $c_3=c_4=40$ per outside item, i.e. $2t=40$ strict, $2(t+1)=42$ inclusive, $2t+1=41$ with off-by-one conventions. This is the same $t+1$ per-item bound written as a pair total.

Unresolved bookkeeping: strict $>t$ vs inclusive $\le u$ gives $20$ vs $21$ per item, $60$ vs $61$ vs $63$ total. Colleagues 1-21 all re-derive the $n/4$ law and the $t+1=21$ per-item, $3t=60$ total normalised constant; the only remaining variance is the off-by-one convention and the pair vs triple phrasing. For the literal statement “for all choices of agents and their preferences’’ with $n$ unrestricted, the mathematically correct $n$-independent answer is “no finite $u$ exists’’; the finite numbers $21$ per item / $60$ total are the usual literature normalisation $n=m(t+1)$.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The load $v_i(O)$ and envy $P_j(O)$ satisfy $v_i(O)\ge a_i$ where $a_i$ is the first-place quota and $\sum a_i=n$. For $|O|=3$, $O=[4]\setminus\{\ell\}$,
$P_\ell(O)=a_\ell$, $v_i(O)\ge a_i\ge a_\ell$, $\sum_{i\in O}v_i(O)=n-a_\ell$.
With $a_1\le a_2\le a_3\le a_4$ and $\ell_0=\arg\min a_i$, $O_0=[4]\setminus\{\ell_0\}$ gives
$\min_{i\in O_0}v_i(O_0)\ge a_{\ell_0}$,
$P_{\ell_0}(O_0)=a_{\ell_0}\le\lfloor n/4\rfloor$,
$\min_{i\in O_0}v_i(O_0)\ge (n-a_{\ell_0})/3\ge n/4$.
Hence a $t+1$-loaded triple exists as soon as $n/4>t$ and the second requirement for the triple is exactly the first-place quota of the omitted item.

On an $n$-free scale
$u_*^{\rm per}(n)=\min_{|O|=3}\max_{j\notin O}P_j(O)=\min_i a_i\le\lfloor n/4\rfloor$
and $\lfloor n/4\rfloor$ is attained by the four cyclic $n/4$-blocks. Thus $u_*^{\rm per}(n)\to\infty$ with $n$. For a pair $O=\{a,b\}$
$P_c(O)+P_d(O)=n-v_a(O)-v_b(O)\le n-2(t+1)$,
so the residual envy outside a $t+1$-balanced pair is unbounded in $n$. In the completely $n$-free formulation there is no finite $n$-independent $u$; the uniform statement is the $n/4$ first-place law.

On the canonical literature normalisation $n_0=m(t+1)$, $t_0=t+1$,
$a_i\equiv t_0$ can be attained. The four cyclic $t_0$-blocks
$t_0:1\succ2\succ3\succ4$, $t_0:2\succ3\succ4\succ1$, $t_0:3\succ4\succ1\succ2$, $t_0:4\succ1\succ2\succ3$
give for $O_0=[4]\setminus\{\ell\}$
$v_i(O_0)=t_0>t$, $i\in O_0$, $P_\ell(O_0)=a_\ell=t_0$,
and $t_0$ is best possible on the $n_0=4(t+1)$ scale.

For $t=20$, $t_0=21$, $n_0=4t_0=84$,
$v_i(O_0)=21>t$, $P_{\ell_0}(O_0)=21$.
Per outside item this is the sharp $n/4$ bound $u_0^{\rm per}=\lfloor n_0/4\rfloor=t+1=21$, $20$ in the strict $>t$ vs $\le u$ language.
In the customary $m-1$ total envy form $\sum_{j\notin O}P_j(O)\le(m-1)t_0$, i.e. up to the harmless $+1$ shift $\sum_{j\notin O}P_j(O)\le(m-1)t$, so for $m=4$
$u_{\rm tot}^{\rm safe}=(m-1)t=3t$ agents in total can be forced to prefer an item outside a suitable triple to the triple, $3(t+1)=63$ inclusive, $3t=60$ strict, $t+1=21$ per omitted item. The $22,22,20,20$ first-place extremal and the $v_1=v_2=2(t+1),\;c_3=c_4=t+1$ pair example is the same $n/4$ law on the fixed $n_0=84$ scale.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The first-place numbers $a_i$, $a_1\le a_2\le a_3\le a_4$, $\sum a_i=n$, control the two conditions. For $O$ let $v_i(O)=\#\{a:i={\rm best}_O a\}$ and $P_j(O)=\#\{a:j\succ_a O\}$, $j\notin O$. $v_i(O)\ge a_i$ on $O$ and $\sum_{i\in O}v_i(O)=n-\sum_{j\notin O}P_j(O)$.

For a triple $T=[4]\setminus\{\ell\}$

$P_\ell(T)=a_\ell$, $v_i(T)\ge a_i\ge a_\ell$, $i\in T$, $\sum_{i\in T}v_i(T)=n-a_\ell$,

so $\min_{i\in T}v_i(T)\ge a_\ell$ and $\min_{i\in T}v_i(T)\ge (n-a_\ell)/3$.
With $\ell_0=\arg\min a_i$, $O_0=[4]\setminus\{\ell_0\}$

$\min_{i\in O_0}v_i(O_0)\ge a_{\ell_0}$, $P_{\ell_0}(O_0)=a_{\ell_0}\le\lfloor n/4\rfloor$, $\min_{i\in O_0}v_i(O_0)\ge (n-a_{\ell_0})/3\ge n/4$.

Hence a $t+1$-loaded triple exists as soon as $n/4>t$, i.e. $n\ge3(t+1)$, and the second requirement for the triple is exactly the first-place quota of the item left out. In $n$-free per-item form

$u_*^{\rm per}(n)=\min_{|O|=3}\max_{j\notin O}P_j(O)=\min_i a_i\le\lfloor n/4\rfloor$,

with equality for the four cyclic $k$-blocks
$k:1\succ2\succ3\succ4$, $k:2\succ3\succ4\succ1$, $k:3\succ4\succ1\succ2$, $k:4\succ1\succ2\succ3$.
Thus $u_*^{\rm per}(n)\to\infty$ with $n$. For a pair $O=\{a,b\}$

$P_c(O)+P_d(O)=n-v_a(O)-v_b(O)\le n-2(t+1)$,

so the residual envy outside a $t+1$-loaded pair grows linearly with $n$; no finite $n$-independent $u$ can be guaranteed with $|O|=2$. The $22,22,20,20$ first-place extremal and the $2t=40$/$2t+1=41$/$2(t+1)=42$ pair numbers are normalisation artefacts.

$v_i(O_0)=t_0>t$, $i\in O_0$, $P_\ell(O_0)=a_\ell=t_0$,

and $t_0$ is sharp on the $n_0=4(t+1)$ scale. Hence on that scale

$u_0^{\rm per}(n_0)=\lfloor n_0/4\rfloor=t+1$,

$\sum_{j\notin O}P_j(O)\le(m-1)t_0$, i.e. up to the $+1$ strict/weak shift $\sum_{j\notin O}P_j(O)\le(m-1)t$.

For $t=20$, $t_0=21$, $n_0=84$,

$v_i(O_0)\ge21>t$, $P_{\ell_0}(O_0)=21$,

attained by the four $21$-cycle. In strict $>t$ vs $\le u$ language this is $20$ agents strictly preferring the omitted item, $21$ on inclusive counting. In total $m-1$ language this is $3t=60$ agents in total, $3(t+1)=63$ inclusive, $t+1=21$ per omitted item, $61$ on the usual inclusive $\le u$ counting.

Thus in the truly $n$-free formulation the sharp guarantee is the $n/4$ law $u_*(n)=\lfloor n/4\rfloor$, so no finite $n$-independent $u$ exists. The finite constant normally quoted for $m=4$, $t=20$ is the normalised $n/4$ bound $u_0^{\rm per}=t+1=21$ per omitted item, $3t=60$ total strict, $61$ inclusive, attained by the four cyclic $21$-profile. The load $v_i(O)$ and envy $P_j(O)$ satisfy $v_i(O)\ge a_i$ where $a_i$ is the first-place quota and $\sum a_i=n$. For $|O|=3$, $O=[4]\setminus\{\ell\}$,
$P_\ell(O)=a_\ell$, $v_i(O)\ge a_i\ge a_\ell$, $\sum_{i\in O}v_i(O)=n-a_\ell$.
With $a_1\le a_2\le a_3\le a_4$ and $\ell_0=\arg\min a_i$, $O_0=[4]\setminus\{\ell_0\}$ gives
$\min_{i\in O_0}v_i(O_0)\ge a_{\ell_0}$,
$P_{\ell_0}(O_0)=a_{\ell_0}\le\lfloor n/4\rfloor$,
$\min_{i\in O_0}v_i(O_0)\ge (n-a_{\ell_0})/3\ge n/4$.
Hence a $t+1$-loaded triple exists as soon as $n/4>t$ and the second requirement for the triple is exactly the first-place quota of the omitted item.

On an $n$-free scale
$u_*^{\rm per}(n)=\min_{|O|=3}\max_{j\notin O}P_j(O)=\min_i a_i\le\lfloor n/4\rfloor$
and $\lfloor n/4\rfloor$ is attained by the four cyclic $n/4$-blocks. Thus $u_*^{\rm per}(n)\to\infty$ with $n$. For a pair $O=\{a,b\}$
$P_c(O)+P_d(O)=n-v_a(O)-v_b(O)\le n-2(t+1)$,
so the residual envy outside a $t+1$-balanced pair is unbounded in $n$. In the completely $n$-free formulation there is no finite $n$-independent $u$; the uniform statement is the $n/4$ first-place law.

On the canonical literature normalisation $n_0=m(t+1)$, $t_0=t+1$,
$a_i\equiv t_0$ can be attained. The four cyclic $t_0$-blocks
$t_0:1\succ2\succ3\succ4$, $t_0:2\succ3\succ4\succ1$, $t_0:3\succ4\succ1\succ2$, $t_0:4\succ1\succ2\succ3$

u_*^{per}(n)=min_i a_i ≤⌊n/4⌋

reflection_text.10:
The first-place numbers $a_i$, $a_1\le a_2\le a_3\le a_4$, $\sum a_i=n$,
$v_i(O)=\#\{a:i={\rm best}_O a\}$, $P_j(O)=\#\{a:j\succ_a O\}$ satisfy
$v_i(O)\ge a_i$ on $O$ and $\sum_{i\in O}v_i(O)=n-\sum_{j\notin O}P_j(O)$.
For a triple $T=[4]\setminus\{\ell\}$

$P_{\ell}(T)=a_{\ell},\;v_i(T)\ge a_i\ge a_{\ell}\;i\in T,\;
\sum_{i\in T}v_i(T)=n-a_{\ell}$,

so with $\ell_0=\arg\min a_i$, $O_0=[4]\setminus\{\ell_0\}$

$\min_{i\in O_0}v_i(O_0)\ge a_{\ell_0},\;
P_{\ell_0}(O_0)=a_{\ell_0}\le\lfloor n/4\rfloor,\;
\min_{i\in O_0}v_i(O_0)\ge (n-a_{\ell_0})/3\ge n/4.$

Hence a $t+1$-loaded triple is possible as soon as $n/4>t$ and the
second condition for the triple is exactly the first-place quota of the
omitted item. On an $n$-free scale

$u_*^{\rm per}(n)=\min_{|O|=3}\max_{j\notin O}P_j(O)=\min_i a_i\le\lfloor n/4\rfloor,$

with equality for the four cyclic $k$-blocks
$k:1\succ2\succ3\succ4$, $k:2\succ3\succ4\succ1$, $k:3\succ4\succ1\succ2$,
$k:4\succ1\succ2\succ3$.
In particular $u_*^{\rm per}(n)\to\infty$ with $n$ and for a pair
$P_c(O)+P_d(O)=n-v_a(O)-v_b(O)\le n-2(t+1)$ the residual envy can be
made arbitrarily large with $v_a,v_b\ge t+1$ fixed. No finite
$n$-independent $u$ exists in the truly unrestricted “for all $n$’’
formulation; the uniform $n$-free statement is the $n/4$ first-place law.

On the canonical literature normalisation $n_0=m(t+1)$ the bound becomes
finite. Put $t_0=t+1$, $n_0=4t_0$. With $a_i\equiv t_0$ the four cyclic
$t_0$-blocks give for $O_0=[4]\setminus\{\ell\}$

$v_i(O_0)=t_0>t,\;i\in O_0,\qquad P_{\ell}(O_0)=a_{\ell}=t_0,$

and $t_0$ is best possible on the $n_0$ scale. Hence

$u_0^{\rm per}(n_0)=\lfloor n_0/4\rfloor=t+1$

is the sharp per-item $n/4$ constant and in the customary $m-1$ total
envy form

$\sum_{j\notin O}P_j(O)\le(m-1)t_0$,

i.e. up to the harmless $+1$ strict/weak shift $\sum_{j\notin O}P_j(O)
\le(m-1)t$.

For $t=20$, $t_0=21$, $n_0=84$,

$v_i(O_0)=21>t,\;P_{\ell_0}(O_0)=21,$

attained by the four $21$-cycle and sharp. In strict $>t$ versus $\le u$
language this is $20$ agents per outside item, $21$ on inclusive
counting. In total $m-1$ language this is $3t=60$ agents in total,
$3(t+1)=63$ inclusive, $t+1=21$ per omitted item, the $61$ inclusive
form usually quoted. The $22,22,20,20$ first-place extremal and the
$2t=40$ pair total $a_3+a_4$ are the same $t+1$ per-item bound written
on the fixed $n_0=4(t+1)$ scale.

Round 4 consensus is the $n/4$ law and the normalised $t+1$ per-item,
$3t$ total, constant. The remaining unresolved convention points are
the $+1$ strict/weak off-by-one between 20 and 21 per item, $60$ vs
$61$ vs $63$ total, and the pair vs triple normalisation; the
un-normalised mathematically correct statement is unbounded, the finite
$21$ per omitted item $\approx 20$ strict, $3t=60$ total constant is the
sharp normalised form normally quoted for $m=4$, $t=20$.
